src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:1211-1216 _small_result_to_markdown returns None whenever len(rows) != 1, so any multi-row (>=2) DATAFRAME payload never takes the text-line path. In components_to_blocks (lines 330-337), when _small_result_to_markdown returns None the code appends {"type": "table", **payload} exactly as before this change, using the unmodified _build_table_payload/_compute_table_payload pipeline. git show d115edb:src/sqllens/tools/_format.py confirms _small_result_to_markdown/_SMALL_RESULT_MAX_COLUMNS did not exist pre-change, so the base behavior for multi-row was the same plain table block. Multi-row output is therefore unchanged.

src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:46 defines _SMALL_RESULT_MAX_COLUMNS = 4. _small_result_to_markdown (lines 1200-1216) returns None when len(columns) > _SMALL_RESULT_MAX_COLUMNS (the `not 1 <= len(columns) <= _SMALL_RESULT_MAX_COLUMNS` guard on line 1214). In components_to_blocks (lines 330-337), when _small_result_to_markdown returns None, the code falls through to `candidates.append({"type": "table", **payload})` — identical to the pre-feature table-block path. So a 1-row, 5+ column payload takes the table branch unchanged.

src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:1200-1223 _small_result_to_markdown returns None when payload.get('truncated', 0) != 0 (line 1213), so a 1-row payload with truncated==1 fails the guard and the function returns None. The caller (components_to_blocks/_serialize_blocks_to_markdown path) then falls through to the normal table block, rendered by _table_block_to_markdown (line 1226), which is the same rendering path used before the small-result feature was added. Thus a 1-row, truncated==1 payload produces the same table block as before.

components_to_blocks builds `candidates` in a single forward pass over the component stream (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:314-424); each DATAFRAME component appends either a `result_text` candidate (one-row/small result) or a `table` candidate at that same stream position (lines 330-343), interleaved with `text` and `chart` candidates in stream order. The final block-building loop (lines 444-455) iterates `candidates` in that identical order and converts `result_text` to a public `{"type": "text", ...}` block in place (lines 450-453), appending non-text/result_text candidates (chart, unmarked-filtered text) unchanged in the same pass. No reordering step separates table/text/chart candidates before this loop, so the resulting text block sits in the same relative position among surrounding text/chart blocks that a table block would have occupied.

_build_table_payload (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:907-908) builds columns/rows via _coerce_cell(c) and _coerce_cell(row.get(c, "")) into the payload dict. That same payload is passed to _small_result_to_markdown (called at line 333 with `payload` from `_build_table_payload(rich)`), which at lines 1217-1220 does `_escape_small_result_text(val)` for `val` in `rows[0]` -- i.e. it escapes the already-coerced cell strings from the payload, not raw values. This confirms each value rendered in the text block is exactly the _coerce_cell string the table block would have held, before the additional Markdown escaping applied only for the text-block rendering.

src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:49 defines _SMALL_RESULT_ESCAPED_CHARS = frozenset("\\`*_[]<>~|&") — exactly the set \ ` * _ [ ] < > ~ | & claimed. _escape_small_result_text (lines 1192-1197) replaces \r and \n each with a single space (line 1194: value.replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ")), then backslash-escapes each character in that set (lines 1195-1197). This is applied to both column names and values in _small_result_to_markdown (line 1218), which would render `*x* [a](b)` as literal escaped text rather than Markdown emphasis/link syntax.

In components_to_blocks (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py), each DATAFRAME component is handled independently in the forward pass (lines 330-343): _build_table_payload builds the payload, _small_result_to_markdown (line 1200) checks it qualifies as a one-row/<=4-column/untruncated result, and if so appends a distinct {"type": "result_text", "text": small} candidate (line 335) tagged with nothing that would allow cross-candidate merging. In the second pass (lines 444-455), every 'result_text' candidate is unconditionally converted to a public {"type": "text", ...} block and appended to `blocks` (lines 450-453) -- there is no dedup, no last-wins collapsing, and no merging logic applied to result_text candidates (unlike the explicit last-wins handling for TEXT components). Two DATAFRAME components in one turn that each qualify as one-row results therefore each produce their own text block, preserved at their own position in stream order (blocks list built by iterating candidates in original order).

In src/sqllens/tools/_format.py, _small_result_to_markdown (lines 1200-1223) returns the '**column:** value' lines (or bullet list for >1 column) only when len(rows)==1, payload['truncated']==0, and 1<=len(columns)<=_SMALL_RESULT_MAX_COLUMNS (=4, line 46). _small_result_to_markdown (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:1200-1223) builds each line via _escape_small_result_text(col) and _escape_small_result_text(val) (line 1218). _escape_small_result_text (line 1192-1197) calls value.replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ") at line 1194, which requires value to already be a str (int/None have no .replace). The payload's columns and rows[0] are populated exclusively via _coerce_cell, which unconditionally returns str(value) (line 802-805: 'return str(value)'). _build_table_payload (line 874) delegates to _compute_table_payload (line 895), which sets str_columns = [_coerce_cell(c) for c in columns] (line 907) and coerced_rows = [[_coerce_cell(row.get(c, "")) for c in columns] for row in rows] (line 908), and returns payload['columns']=str_columns, and rows built from coerced_rows. The only caller of _small_result_to_markdown (line 333) passes payload = _build_table_payload(rich) (line 331), so the payload it receives always has str columns/cells, confirming the claim that _coerce_cell guarantees str and _small_result_to_markdown depends on that (via _escape_small_result_text's .replace call) rather than handling None or non-str values directly.

_format.py:1192-1197 _escape_small_result_text backslash-escapes chars in _SMALL_RESULT_ESCAPED_CHARS = frozenset("\\`*_[]<>~|&") (line 49) and flattens \r/\n to spaces, so a value can never contain a real line break. _small_result_to_markdown (1217-1223) always renders a value as `**{col}:** {value}` (single column) or `- **{col}:** {value}` (multi-column list), so the escaped value's first character is always preceded by the label/bullet text on the same line, never at true line-start. CommonMark block-level constructs (ATX '#' heading, list markers '-'/'+'/'digit.', setext '=' underline, blockquote) all require the marker at line-start, which never occurs here. Inline markup that could use unescaped '(' or '!' (links/images) requires an unescaped '[' immediately after, but '[' and ']' are in the escaped set, so '!(' and '(' alone produce no markup. The renderer (src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html:753) configures markdown-it with linkify:false and typographer:false, so no autolinking or smart-punctuation path could independently turn these characters into markup. All claimed conditions verified.

Traced a single row too large to fit the budget through src/sqllens/tools/_format.py. _compute_table_payload (lines 895-950) does a binary search on the row prefix; for one oversized row it lands at rows=[], row_count=0, truncated=1 (columns/header-only form is kept unless even that exceeds the byte cap, in which case None is returned and no table block is emitted at all). _small_result_to_markdown (lines 1200-1216) explicitly bails to None when payload['truncated'] != 0, so the one-row special case never fires for a truncated row. _table_block_to_markdown (lines 1226-1245) then renders only the header + separator (rows list is empty) plus, since total(1) is not > _MAX_ROWS_RENDERED, no 'Showing first N of M' footer at all. The widget (src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html lines 405-473) mirrors this: with state.columns.length truthy but rows empty it renders only the <thead> header row and a 'showing 0 of 0 (1 truncated)' meta span (lines 443-446) -- counts only, no cell values. In both serializers the only things that leak are column names and row counts, never any cell value, matching the prompt line under scrutiny.

Prompt text (default.py:67-68) says: single row with four or fewer columns shown as short text; more than four columns or more than one row shown as table. Code predicate in _small_result_to_markdown (_format.py:1210-1214) requires len(rows)==1, truncated==0, and 1 <= len(columns) <= _SMALL_RESULT_MAX_COLUMNS (=4, line 46). Zero-column case: predicate requires len(columns)>=1, so a zero-column one-row payload fails the predicate and falls through to the table path, consistent with the claim that the prompt doesn't mention zero columns and such a payload stays a table.

src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:49,1192-1218 backslash-escapes DB values/columns for chars in frozenset("\\`*_[]<>~|&") and builds `**col:** value` lines (line 1218). These land in text blocks rendered by renderTextBlock (query_results.html:772-785), which lazily builds the renderer via createMarkdownRenderer (query_results.html:752-753) with markdownit({html:false, linkify:false, typographer:false, breaks:true}). All escaped characters (\, `, *, _, [, ], <, >, ~, |, &) are ASCII punctuation per CommonMark's backslash-escape rule, so markdown-it (CommonMark-compliant) renders each as the literal character rather than parsing it as markdown syntax or (for <, &) as raw HTML/entities. The comment block at query_results.html:739-751 accurately describes html:false (raw HTML escaped, safe for innerHTML), validateLink, no images, and breaks:true -- all verified against the actual config object and renderer rule overrides (table_open/table_close, link_open) in the same function.
